intro: Mosiah 24 tells the story of **Alma and his people in bondage**. Amulon, the leader of King Noah's former priests, wins favour with the Lamanite king **Laman**, who appoints him and his brethren as teachers over the Lamanite lands. They teach the **language of Nephi** and writing, but not the law of Moses or the words of Abinadi, and the Lamanites grow rich, cunning and powerful. Amulon then turns on Alma — who had once been a fellow priest and had believed Abinadi — and sets **taskmasters** over his people, forbidding even their prayers on pain of death. Praying silently in their hearts, the people hear the **voice of the Lord**: He will **ease their burdens** so that they cannot feel them on their backs, and in time deliver them. The burdens are made light, the people **submit cheerfully and with patience**, and at last the Lord sends a **deep sleep** on the Lamanites. Alma's people escape by night, give thanks in the **valley of Alma**, and after twelve days in the wilderness are received with joy by **King Mosiah in Zarahemla**.
reading_tip: This chapter leans heavily on **compound verbs** (noun or adjective + `کردن` / `شدن` / `دادن` / `نمودن`): `تعیین کردن` "to appoint", `تصرّف کردن` "to take possession of", `رهایی دادن` "to deliver", `سبک کردن` "to make light". It also uses the **passive with `شدن`**, the **pluperfect** (`کرده بود`, `نهاده شده بودند`), the **future** with `خواه-` in the Lord's promises, **`شروع … نمودن`** "to begin to …", and **imperatives** (`بگیرید`, `باشید`, `برو`, `شتاب کن`). When you meet a noun followed by `کرد`, `شد` or `داد`, read the two words together as one verb before translating the sentence.

forms.note: Persian writes numbers with the Indo-Persian digits `۰ ۱ ۲ ۳ ۴ ۵ ۶ ۷ ۸ ۹`. Each number's pronunciation is introduced where it first appears in this chapter (verse numbers included).

The teens 10–19 (`دَه` _dah_, `یازده` _yāzdah_ …) and the multiples of ten (`بیست` _bīst_ 20 …) are single words, not digit-by-digit composites; other two-digit numbers join tens and units with `و` _o_ "and": `بیست و چهار` _bīst-o-čahār_ "twenty-four".

entries.title: Grammar: چنین گذشت — "and it came to pass"
entries.body: The narrative formula `و چنین گذشت که` _o čonīn gozašt ke_ calques the English Book of Mormon's "and it came to pass that": `چنین` "thus" + `گذشت` "(it) passed" + the complementizer `که` "that". It marks the start of a new event and carries no meaning of its own. Mosiah 24 uses it eight times; with `اینک` "now" it becomes `و اینک چنین گذشت که` "and now it came to pass that".

entries.title: Grammar: Ezafe chains
entries.body: The ezafe `-e` (after a vowel `-ye`) links a noun to whatever modifies or possesses it, and the links can be chained: each noun but the last takes the ezafe. The publisher rarely writes it on consonant-final words, so it is marked editorially here. `در چشمان پادشاه لامانیان` is _dar češmān-e pādšāh-e Lāmāniyān_ "in the eyes of the king of the Lamanites": eyes ← of the king ← of the Lamanites.

entries.title: Grammar: Compound verbs and the pluperfect
entries.body:
Most "verbs" in this chapter are **compound verbs**: a noun or adjective carrying the meaning, plus a light verb (`کردن` "do", `شدن` "become", `دادن` "give", `نمودن` "do") carrying tense and person. `تصرّف کردن` (lit. "do possession") = "to take possession of"; `تعیین کردن` ("do appointment") = "to appoint". Swapping `کردن` for `شدن` gives the passive-like sense: `تصرّف شده بود` "had been possessed".

The **pluperfect** ("had done") is the light verb's past participle + past of `بودن`: `کرده بودند` "they had done", `کرده بود` "he had done".

entries.title: Grammar: The passive with شدن
entries.body: Persian forms the passive from the **past participle** of the main verb + `شدن` "to become", which carries tense and person: `خوانده می شد` "he was (being) called" (lit. "became called"). The participle alone, with `شده`, works like an English participial phrase: `خوانده شده بنام پدرش` "being called after the name of his father".

forms.desc: `بدست` _be-dast_ "into the hand(s) (of), by" — `به` + `دست` written as one word: `بدست مردمش` "by his people" ([verse 4](#verse-4)); `بدست گرفتن` "to take control of" ([verse 8](#verse-8), [verse 9](#verse-9))

etym.prose: contraction of [`به‌-`](../word_formation.html#be-in-with-by) _be_ "to, by" + `این` _īn_ "this".

forms.note: `بدین گونه` _bedīn gūne_ "in this way, thus" ([verse 4](#verse-4), [verse 7](#verse-7))

etym.prose: transliteration of English _Nephi_, the Book of Mormon prophet's name. Sometimes connected to Egyptian _nfr_ "good, fair" or to Hebrew, but Persian here just spells the English form phonetically.

forms.note: `در میان` _dar mīyān-e_ "among" ([verse 4](#verse-4), [verse 7](#verse-7))

entries.meaning: beginning, start — شروع کردن / شروع به … نمودن: to begin

etym.prose: from Arabic _šurūʿ_ "commencement," root š-r-ʿ.

forms.note: `شروع به … نمودن` / `شروع نمودن` + infinitive "to begin to …" ([verse 7](#verse-7), [verse 8](#verse-8), [verse 10](#verse-10)); see [Grammar: شروع … نمودن](#grammar-to-begin-to)

etym.prose: `آموز-` (pres. stem of `آموختن` "to teach/learn") + [`-ش`](../word_formation.html#e-verbal-noun-from-the-present-stem) (nominalizer).

entries.title: Grammar: شروع … نمودن — "to begin to …"
entries.body: "To begin to do X" is `شروع کردن` / `شروع نمودن` (`نمودن` is the formal twin of `کردن`) with the activity as an **infinitive** or verbal noun, usually introduced by `به`: `شروع به آموزش دادن شد` "began to be taught". The infinitive may also follow the light verb instead: `شروع نمود … بدست گرفتن` "began to take …". With a passive sense, `شد` replaces `نمود`.

examples.persian: زبان{e} نیفای ... شروع به آموزش دادن شد
examples.translit: zabān-e Nīfāy ... šorūʿ be āmūzeš dādan šod
examples.en: the language of Nephi began to be taught

examples.persian: لامانیان شروع به افزایش{e} ثروت نمودند
examples.translit: Lāmāniyān šorūʿ be afzāyeš-e ṯarvat namūdand
examples.en: the Lamanites began to increase in riches

examples.persian: آنها شروع نمودند به درگاه{e} خدا توانمندانه زاری کردن
examples.translit: ānhā šorūʿ namūdand be dargāh-e xodā tavānmandāne zārī kardan
examples.en: they began to cry mightily to God

forms.note: `با یکدیگر` _bā yekdīgar_ "with one another" ([verse 5](#verse-5), [verse 7](#verse-7)); `به یکدیگر` "to one another" ([verse 6](#verse-6))

entries.meaning: friendly, amicable; in a friendly way

etym.prose: `دوست` _dūst_ "friend" + the adjective/adverb suffix [`-انه`](../word_formation.html#the-adverb-adjective-suffix-ne) _-āne_ "in the manner of".

entries.meaning: existence, being — با این وجود: nevertheless

etym.prose: from Arabic _wujūd_ "existence," root w-j-d "to find, exist."

forms.note: `با این وجود` _bā īn vojūd_ "nevertheless" (lit. "with this existence") ([verse 5](#verse-5)); cf. `با این حال` ([verse 9](#verse-9))

etym.prose: Middle Persian _xwadāy_ "lord, master" (← Old Iranian _xwa-tāwya-_ "self-powerful"); the ordinary Persian word for God.

forms.desc: `خدایشان` _xodā-yešān_ "their God" — the glide `ی` comes between `خدا` and the suffix ([verse 5](#verse-5), [verse 12](#verse-12), [verse 21](#verse-21), [verse 22](#verse-22))

entries.meaning: to know (a person), be acquainted with; to recognize

forms.desc: neg. 3pl past impf. `نمی شناختند` _nemī-šenāxtand_ "they did not know" ([verse 5](#verse-5))

forms.note: `شناختن` is "to know" a person or thing by acquaintance; `دانستن` (verse 14) is "to know" a fact.

entries.meaning: no; not (in short answers and rhetorical questions)

entries.title: Grammar: نه … نه … — "neither … nor …"
entries.body: Repeating `نه` _na_ before each item gives "neither … nor …". Persian may keep the verb itself positive (`می گفتند` "they were saying") because the `نه` already supplies the negation; colloquial Persian usually also negates the verb.

examples.persian: نه به آنها دربارۀ سَروَر خدایشان هیچ چیزی می گفتند، نه از قانون{e} موسی
examples.translit: na be ānhā darbāre-ye Sarvar xodā-yešān hīč čīz-ī mī-goftand, na az qānūn-e Mūsā
examples.en: neither did they teach them anything concerning the Lord their God, neither the law of Moses

etym.prose: `در` _dar_ "in" + `باره` _bāre_ "matter, regard" → "in the matter of".

entries.meaning: any (in negative clauses: "not any, nothing at all")

forms.note: `هیچ چیزی` "anything / nothing", `هیچ کسی` "anyone / no one" — with a negative or `نه` it means "no …, none" ([verse 5](#verse-5), [verse 21](#verse-21))

entries.meaning: to say (past _گفت goft_; archaic narrative _گفتا goftā_)

forms.note: Suppletive present stem `گو` _gū-_ (`گویند` _gūyand_); archaic narrative `گفتا` _goftā_ "saying".

etym.prose: from Arabic _qānūn_ "law, rule," ultimately from Greek _kanōn_ "rule, canon."
from Hebrew _Mōšeh_, traditionally "drawn out (of water)," via Arabic `موسیٰ`.

forms.note: `سخن گفتن` "to speak" ([verse 22](#verse-22))

entries.meaning: Abinadi (the prophet burned by King Noah)

etym.prose: Persian transliteration of English _Abinadi_; sometimes linked to Hebrew _ʾăbî_ "my father" + _nādîv_ "noble, generous".
from Arabic, originally "guardian, friend"; in Persian shifted to a contrastive conjunction.
past participle of the literary `نگاشتن` negāštan "to write, inscribe" (pres. `نگار` negār-), used as a noun.

entries.family: نگاشتن _negāštan_ to write, inscribe; نگارش _negāreš_ writing, style

forms.note: `خود` after a noun means "(one's) own": `نگاشته های خود` "their own records", `سرهای خود` "your heads"; with a possessive suffix it is the reflexive "-self".

etym.prose: from Arabic _ṯabt_ "firm, fixed", root ṯ-b-t "to be firm".
`این` _īn_ "this" + `که` _ke_ "that" → "the [fact] that".
`افزا` _afzā-_ (present stem of `افزودن` "to add, increase") + [`-یش`](../word_formation.html#e-verbal-noun-from-the-present-stem) (verbal-noun suffix, with glide `ی`).
from Arabic _ṯarwa_ "wealth," root ṯ-r-w "to be wealthy."

entries.meaning: to show; (formal light verb) to do, perform (synonym of کردن in formal prose)

forms.note: `نمودن` is a formal synonym of `کردن` as a light verb; in this chapter it pairs with `شروع` "beginning".

etym.prose: `داد` _dād_ "giving" (past stem of `دادن`) + `و` + `ستد` _sotad_ "taking" (past stem of archaic `ستدن` "to take") → "give-and-take".

forms.note: `شروع به داد و ستد با یکدیگر نمودند` "they began to trade one with another" ([verse 7](#verse-7))

etym.prose: Arabic `قدرت` _qodrat_ "power" + Persian [`-مند`](../word_formation.html#the-suffix-mand) _-mand_ "possessing".
`خرد` _xerad_ (wisdom, intellect) + [`-مند`](../word_formation.html#the-suffix-mand) (possessing) + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i) suffix.

forms.desc: written `خرَدمندی` with a fatha over `ر` to show the reading _xeradmandī_ ([verse 7](#verse-7))

etym.prose: Middle Persian _gēhān_ "world"; originally "that which moves/lives."

Arabic `حیله` _ḥīle_ "trick, ruse" + Persian [`-گر`](../word_formation.html#gar-one-who-works-with-or-practices-x) _-gar_ "one who practises X" → "trickster". The publisher writes the two parts as separate words.
`خرد` _xerad_ "wisdom, intellect" + [`-مند`](../word_formation.html#the-suffix-mand) _-mand_ "possessing".

forms.desc: written `خرَدمند` with a fatha to show _xeradmand_ ([verse 7](#verse-7))

entries.meaning: many, much, very, a great deal

etym.prose: [`نا-`](../word_formation.html#n-un-non-in) + [`بکار`](../word_formation.html#be-in-with-by) ([به‌-](../word_formation.html#be-in-with-by) + `کار` "work") + `-ی` ([abstract suffix](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-g)) → "non-useful-ness, wickedness".

entries.family: [`نا-`](../word_formation.html#n-un-non-in) _nā-_ (privative prefix); `کار` _kār_ "work" (an entry in this chapter); `نابکار` _nābekār_ "wicked, useless" (the underlying adjective).

etym.prose: probably from Turkic _čapavul_ "raid" (cf. Turkish _çapul_), borrowed in the Mongol period.
`دل` _del_ "heart" + `شاد` _šād_ "happy" → "glad of heart".

forms.note: `مگر اینکه` _magar īnke_ "unless, except" ([verse 7](#verse-7))

entries.title: Grammar: Infinitives as verb complements
entries.body: The Persian infinitive (`-dan` / `-tan`) works like a verbal noun. After `شروع نمودن` "to begin" it names the action begun, and it can carry its own complements, which come **before** it: `مردمی حیله گر و خرَدمند شدن` "to become a cunning and wise people", `اختیار … را بدست گرفتن` "to take authority".

examples.persian: شروع نمودند ... مردمی حیله گر و خرَدمند شدن
examples.translit: šorūʿ namūdand ... mardom-ī ḥīlegar o xeradmand šodan
examples.en: began to be a cunning and a wise people

examples.persian: شروع نمود اختیار بر آلما و برادرانش را بدست گرفتن
examples.translit: šorūʿ namūd extiyār bar Ālmā o barādarān-aš rā be-dast gereftan
examples.en: began to exercise authority over Alma and his brethren

entries.meaning: authority, control, power; choice, free will

etym.prose: from Arabic _ixtiyār_ "choice", root x-y-r "good; to choose" (pattern _iftiʿāl_).

forms.note: `اختیار بر … را بدست گرفتن` "to take authority over, exercise authority over" ([verse 8](#verse-8), [verse 9](#verse-9))

etym.prose: the preverb `وا` _vā-_ + `داشتن` _dāštan_ "to have, hold".

forms.desc: 3sg past `واداشت` _vādāšt_ "he caused", followed by `که` or `تا` + subjunctive ([verse 8](#verse-8), [verse 19](#verse-19))

entries.family: `وادار کردن` _vādār kardan_ "to force, compel" (the everyday equivalent).

etym.prose: `یک` _yek_ "one" + indefinite _-ī_ → "one [of them]".
from Syriac _qaššīšā_ "elder, presbyter"; the usual Persian word for a Christian priest.

entries.meaning: front, presence; equal — در برابر / از برابر: before, in front of
to drive, propel; to drive out, expel

etym.prose: Middle Persian _rāndan_ "to drive"; `بیرون راندن` = "to drive out."
`خشم` _xašm_ (anger, wrath) + [`-گین`](../word_formation.html#the-suffix-gin) (laden-with suffix).
from Arabic _muṭīʿ_ "obeying", root ṭ-w-ʿ "to obey".
from Arabic, root ḥ-w-l "to change, turn".

entries.meaning: to pull, draw; to stretch, extend

forms.desc: 3sg past impf. `می کشید` _mī-kešīd_ — `از آنها کار می کشید` "he was working them, exacting labour from them" ([verse 9](#verse-9))

etym.prose: `کار` _kār_ "work" + `فرما` _farmā-_ (present stem of `فرمودن` "to command") → "one who orders the work".

entries.meaning: to place, put, set; (نام نهادن) to name
entries.family: نهاد _nahād_ nature, institution; بنیان‌ نهادن _bonyān nahādan_ to found

forms.desc: pp. `نهاده` _nahāde_ — `نهاده بود` "he had placed" ([verse 9](#verse-9)); passive `نهاده شده اند` ([verse 14](#verse-14)), `نهاده شده بودند` ([verse 15](#verse-15))

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 10 (`ده` — a single word, not "one-zero")

forms.note: `رنج های آنها` "their afflictions" ([verse 10](#verse-10)); `رنج هایشان` "their afflictions" ([verse 13](#verse-13), [verse 14](#verse-14))
`چنان … که …` "so … that …": `چنان زیاد بود که` "was so great that" ([verse 10](#verse-10), [verse 16](#verse-16))

entries.meaning: threshold, gateway; the (royal or divine) presence, court

etym.prose: `در` "door" + [`گاه`](../word_formation.html#g-h-place-or-time-of-x) "place, time" → "door-place, threshold."

`توان` _tavān_ "power, ability" + [`-مند`](../word_formation.html#the-suffix-mand) _-mand_ "possessing" → `توانمند` "powerful", + [`-انه`](../word_formation.html#the-adverb-adjective-suffix-ne) _-āne_ → "powerfully".

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 11 (`یازده` — a single word, not "one-one")
to take up, pick up, take away, remove

forms.desc: 3pl subj. `بردارند` _bardārand_ — `از زاری کردن دست بردارند` "(that) they stop crying out" (`دست برداشتن از` "to take one's hand off" → "to stop") ([verse 11](#verse-11))

etym.prose: `نگه` _negah_ "watch, keeping" + [`-بان`](../word_formation.html#b-n-keeper-watcher-of-x) _-bān_ "keeper of".
from Arabic _murāqib_ "observer", root r-q-b "to watch".

forms.note: `مراقب … بودن` "to watch (over), keep an eye on": `تا مراقب آنها باشند` "to watch them" ([verse 11](#verse-11))

entries.title: Grammar: The subjunctive after تا and که
entries.body: Clauses of purpose and of commands or wishes take the **subjunctive**. `تا` "so that" and `که` "that" after verbs like `فرمان دادن` "to command" or `واداشتن` "to cause" introduce it. Simple verbs take `بـ-` (`بنویسند`, `بدانید`); compound verbs and `بودن` usually do not (`دست بردارند`, `باشند`, `کشته شود`).

examples.persian: به آنها فرمان داد که از زاری کردن دست بردارند
examples.translit: be ānhā farmān dād ke az zārī kardan dast bardārand
examples.en: commanded them that they should stop their cries

examples.persian: نگهبانانی بر آنها نهاد تا مراقب{e} آنها باشند
examples.translit: negahbānān-ī bar ānhā nahād tā morāqeb-e ānhā bāšand
examples.en: he put guards over them to watch them

examples.persian: و اینکه به یکدیگر بنویسند
examples.translit: o īnke be yekdīgar benevīsand
examples.en: and that they might write one to another

entries.meaning: person, individual (literary; in everyday speech replaced by `نفر`)

forms.desc: indef. `کسی` _kas-ī_ "someone, anyone" — `هر کسی که` "whoever" ([verse 11](#verse-11)); `هیچ کسی` "no one" ([verse 21](#verse-21))

etym.prose: native Persian preverb meaning "across, beyond"; cognate with Latin _prae-_, English _fore-_.

forms.note: `فرا خواندن` _farā xāndan_ "to call upon, summon" ([verse 11](#verse-11))
`پیدا شدن` "to be found, appear" ([verse 11](#verse-11))

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 12 (`دوازده` — a single word, not "one-two")

forms.note: `صدا را بلند کردن` "to raise one's voice" ([verse 12](#verse-12), [verse 22](#verse-22))

etym.prose: Middle Persian _bwland_ "high"; `دست بلند کردن` = "to lift a hand (against)."

entries.meaning: heart, mind; inner seat of feeling and thought

forms.note: `دل هایشان` _del-hā-yešān_ "their hearts" ([verse 12](#verse-12))
`برون ریختن` "to pour out": `دل هایشان را … برون ریختند` "they poured out their hearts" ([verse 12](#verse-12)), `سپاس هایشان را … برون ریختند` ([verse 21](#verse-21))
`از … آگاه بودن` "to know of, be aware of" ([verse 12](#verse-12), [verse 13](#verse-13))

entries.title: Grammar: Possessive suffixes
entries.body: Possession is usually shown by an enclitic suffix: `-am` "my", `-at` "your (sg.)", `-aš` "his/her", `-emān` "our", `-etān` "your (pl.)", `-ešān` "their". After a vowel the plural ones drop their `-e-` and a glide `ی` is written: `خدا` → `خدایشان` _xodā-yešān_, `صدا` → `صدایشان`, `ها` → `هایشان`. After a consonant they attach directly: `مردمش`, `فرزندانشان`, `راهشان`. The publisher sometimes writes `شان` as a separate word (`غلّه شان`).

examples.persian: آلما و مردمش صدایشان را به سَروَر خدایشان بلند نکردند
examples.translit: Ālmā o mardom-aš ṣedā-yešān rā be Sarvar xodā-yešān boland nakardand
examples.en: Alma and his people did not raise their voices to the Lord their God

examples.persian: گلّه هایشان و همچنین غلّه شان
examples.translit: galle-hā-yešān o hamčonīn ġalle-šān
examples.en: their flocks, and also of their grain

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 13 (`سیزده` — a single word, not "one-three")
call, voice, cry — ندای روح: the voice of the Spirit

etym.prose: from Arabic _nidāʾ_ "call, cry," root n-d-w/y.

entries.meaning: archaic narrative past of `گفتن` "saying"; see [Grammar: The archaic narrative گفتا](#grammar-the-archaic-narrative)

entries.title: Grammar: The archaic narrative گفتا
entries.body: `گفتا` _goft-ā_ is an old literary form of `گفت` "(he) said" with the narrative suffix `-ā`. The Persian Book of Mormon uses it where English has "saying:" to introduce quoted speech, here the voice of the Lord.

examples.persian: ندای سَروَر در رنج هایشان بر آنها آمد، گفتا
examples.translit: nedā-ye Sarvar dar ranj-hā-yešān bar ānhā āmad, goftā
examples.en: the voice of the Lord came to them in their afflictions, saying

forms.desc: pl. `سرهای` _sar-hā-ye_ — `سرهای خود را بالا بگیرید` "lift up your heads" ([verse 13](#verse-13))

etym.prose: native Persian; cognate with `والا` _vālā_ "exalted".

light_verb.meaning: to be relieved, set at ease

etym.prose: past participle of `آسودن` āsūdan "to rest, be at ease."

forms.note: `آسوده باشید` "be of good comfort" ([verse 13](#verse-13), [verse 16](#verse-16))

entries.title: Grammar: The imperative
entries.body: The imperative is the present stem with the prefix `بـ-`: singular bare (`ببر` _bebar_ "take!"), plural with `-īd` (`بگیرید` _begīrīd_ "hold!"). Before a stem in `o` the prefix becomes `بُ-`: `برو` _boro_ "go!". `بودن` uses `باش-` without `بـ-` (`باشید` "be!"), and compound verbs drop `بـ-` (`شتاب کن` "make haste!").

examples.persian: سرهای خود را بالا بگیرید و آسوده باشید
examples.translit: sar-hā-ye xod rā bālā begīrīd o āsūde bāšīd
examples.en: lift up your heads and be of good comfort

examples.persian: تو به پیش{e} مردم برو
examples.translit: to be pīš-e mardom boro
examples.en: go thou before the people

examples.persian: شتاب کن و خودت و این مردم را از این سرزمین بیرون ببر
examples.translit: šetāb kon o xod-at o īn mardom rā az īn sarzamīn bīrūn bebar
examples.en: haste thee and get thou and this people out of this land

light_verb.meaning: to make a covenant (lit. "to bind a pact")

etym.prose: Middle Persian _paymān_ "measure, agreement".

forms.desc: `پیمانی` _peymān-ī_ "the covenant (which)" — the `-ī` marks the head of the relative clause ([verse 13](#verse-13))

entries.meaning: to bind, tie, fasten, gird on

forms.desc: pp. `بسته` _baste_ — perfect `بسته اید` "you have made (a covenant)" ([verse 13](#verse-13))
short infinitive `بست` _bast_ after `خواهم`: `پیمان خواهم بست` "I will covenant" ([verse 13](#verse-13))

entries.meaning: to want, wish, desire; (future auxiliary) will

forms.note: As the future auxiliary, `خواه-` is followed by the short (past-stem) infinitive: `خواهم داد` "I will give".

entries.title: Grammar: The future with خواه-
entries.body: The future tense is the present of `خواستن` without `می-` (`خواهم`, `خواهی`, `خواهد` …) followed by the **past stem** of the main verb (the short infinitive): `خواهم داد` _xāham dād_ "I will give". In a compound verb the auxiliary goes between the non-verbal part and the stem: `رهایی خواهم داد` "I will deliver", `سبک خواهم کرد` "I will make light".

examples.persian: من با مردمم پیمان خواهم بست و آنها را از بندگی رهایی خواهم داد
examples.translit: man bā mardom-am peymān xāham bast o ānhā rā az bandegī rahāyī xāham dād
examples.en: I will covenant with my people and deliver them out of bondage

examples.persian: و این را من انجام خواهم داد
examples.translit: o īn rā man anjām xāham dād
examples.en: and this will I do

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 14 (`چهارده` — a single word, not "one-four")

etym.prose: `هم` _ham_ "same" + `چنین` _čonīn_ "such" → "in the same such [way]".

entries.title: Grammar: Relative clauses with -ی که
entries.body: A noun modified by a relative clause usually takes the suffix `-ī` (written `ی`, or `یی` after `ها`), followed by `که` "which, who": `بارهایی که بر شانه های شما نهاده شده اند` "the burdens which are put upon your shoulders". The `را` that marks the whole phrase as direct object comes **after** the relative clause, just before the verb phrase.

examples.persian: بارهایی که بر شانه های شما نهاده شده اند را سبک خواهم کرد
examples.translit: bār-hā-yī ke bar šāne-hā-ye šomā nahāde šode-and rā sabok xāham kard
examples.en: I will ease the burdens which are put upon your shoulders

examples.persian: از پیمانی که شما با من بسته اید آگاهم
examples.translit: az peymān-ī ke šomā bā man baste-īd āgāh-am

`توانستن` is followed by a subjunctive: `بتوانند … تحمل کنند` "(that) they could bear", `نمی توانست … رهایی دهد` "could not deliver".

etym.prose: `حال` ḥāl "state, condition" (Arabic) + `ی` + `که` ke; `در حالیکه` = "in the state that" → "while."
from Arabic, root ḥ-s-s "to sense, perceive" (Form IV).

entries.meaning: accomplishment, end — انجام دادن: to do, perform

forms.note: `از این پس` "hereafter" ([verse 14](#verse-14)); `پس از اینکه` "after" ([verse 25](#verse-25))

etym.prose: from Arabic _ʿunwān_ "title, address".

forms.note: `به عنوان` _be ʿonvān-e_ "as, in the capacity of" — `به عنوان گواهانی برای من` "as witnesses for me" ([verse 14](#verse-14))

entries.meaning: surely, truly, of a certainty; correctly

etym.prose: `به` be "in" + `درستی` dorostī "correctness, truth" (← `درست` dorost "right, true").

entries.meaning: meeting, visit; appearance; (in devotional register) divine visit

light_verb.meaning: to visit, meet; (devotional) to appear to

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 15 (`پانزده` — a single word, not "one-five")

etym.prose: `نیرو` _nīrū_ "strength" + [`-مند`](../word_formation.html#the-suffix-mand) "possessing."
`آسان` _āsān_ "easy" + the abstract suffix [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i).

forms.note: `به آسانی` _be āsānī_ "easily, with ease" ([verse 15](#verse-15))

etym.prose: from Arabic _taḥammul_ "bearing", root ḥ-m-l "to carry" (pattern _tafaʿʿul_). Usually written `تحمّل` with a shadda; the text here omits it.
`شاد` šād "happy" + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i) abstract-noun suffix.

forms.desc: `شادی کنان` _šādī-konān_ "rejoicing, cheerfully" — `شادی کردن` "to rejoice" with the participial suffix [`-ان`](../word_formation.html#n-the-adjectival-present-participle) ([verse 15](#verse-15))

etym.prose: `بردبار` _bordbār_ "patient" (`برد` _bord_ "carried" + `بار` _bār_ "load" → "load-bearing") + the abstract suffix [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i).
← `خواستن` xāstan "to want" (past stem `خواست`); `بر پایۀ خواستِ خود` = "according to his own will."

entries.family: خواستن _xāstan_ to want; خواسته _xāste_ a wish, demand

light_verb.meaning: to submit (to), yield (lit. "to lay down the neck")

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 16 (`شانزده` — a single word, not "one-six")

etym.prose: from Arabic _īmān_ "faith, belief," root ā-m-n "to be secure, believe."
Arabic _ṣabūr_ "very patient" (root ṣ-b-r "to endure") + the Persian abstract suffix [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i).
`دو` _do_ (two) + `باره` _bāre_ (time, occasion). Literally "a second time."

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 17 (`هفده` — a single word, not "one-seven")

forms.note: Present stem `رو` _rav-_; imperative `برو` _boro_ "go!".

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 18 (`هجده` — a single word, not "one-eight")

etym.prose: from Arabic _ṭūl_ "length", root ṭ-w-l "to be long".

forms.note: `در طول` _dar ṭūl-e_ "during, throughout": `در طول شب` "in the night-time", `همۀ طول شب` "all the night-time" ([verse 18](#verse-18))
`گلّه هایشان` _galle-hā-yešān_ "their flocks" ([verse 18](#verse-18))

entries.family: Do not confuse with `غلّه` _ġalle_ "grain" (same verse) — the two differ only in the first letter, `گ` vs `غ`; also distinct from `گله` _gele_ "complaint".

etym.prose: from Arabic `غلّة` "yield, produce," root ġ-l-l.

entries.family: گرد هم آوردن _gerd ham āvardan_ to gather; گِرد _gerd_ (round) is distinct from گَرد _gard_ "dust"

entries.meaning: also, too, even; both (in `هم … هم …` "both … and …")

forms.note: `گرد هم آوردن` _gerd-e ham āvardan_ "to gather together" (lit. "to bring around each other") ([verse 18](#verse-18))

etym.prose: `گرد` _gerd_ "round, together" + `آور` _āvar-_ (present stem of `آوردن` "to bring") + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i) → "bringing together".

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 19 (`نوزده` — a single word, not "one-nine")

entries.warning: The `و` in `خواب` is silent — the word is pronounced _xāb_, not *_xavāb_. Learners may accidentally read it as *_xavāb_.

etym.prose: from Arabic _ʿamīq_ "deep", root ʿ-m-q (pattern _faʿīl_).

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 20 (`بیست` — a single word, not "two-zero")
flowing, in motion; departing, setting out

etym.prose: `روان` "flowing, liquid; soul" + `-ه` → "in the state of flowing."

forms.desc: ezafe form `روانۀ` _ravāne-ye_ — `روانۀ بیابان شدند` "they departed into the wilderness" ([verse 20](#verse-20))

forms.note: `روانه شدن` "to set out, depart" ([verse 20](#verse-20), [verse 24](#verse-24))

etym.prose: `بی` bī "without" + `آب` āb "water" + `ان` -ān → "waterless place."

entries.meaning: when, at the time (that) — هنگامی که

etym.prose: from Arabic, root s-f-r "to travel"; verbal-noun pattern _mufāʿalat_.
Arabic _wādī_ "dry riverbed, valley"; the Persian BoM uses `وادی` as its consistent word for the named valleys Laman and Lemuel.

entries.meaning: to strike, hit, beat; (with various nouns) to perform an action

forms.desc: 3pl past `زدند` _zadand_ — `چادرهایشان را … زدند` "they pitched their tents" ([verse 20](#verse-20))

entries.family: `راهنما` _rāhnamā_ "guide"; `راهنمایی` "guidance" (already introduced); `راهی` "setting out" (already introduced); `راه یافتن` "to find one's way."

etym.prose: `راه` rāh "way, road" + `نما` namā "shower" (← `نمودن` nemūdan "to show") + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i).
`بیست` bīst "20" + `و` o "and" + `یک` yek "1."

forms.note: `سپاس هایشان را … برون ریختند` "they poured out their thanks" ([verse 21](#verse-21))

etym.prose: `مهر` + [`-بان`](../word_formation.html#b-n-keeper-watcher-of-x) "guardian, keeper" (cf. `باغبان` "gardener") → "love-keeper".

forms.note: `جز` + noun: `هیچ کسی جز سَروَر خدایشان` "none except the Lord their God" ([verse 21](#verse-21))

etym.prose: `بیست` _bīst_ "20" + `و` _o_ "and" + `دو` _do_ "2".
`سپاس` sepās "thanks" + `گزار` gozār (← `گزاردن` gozārdan "to render, perform") + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i).
`ستای-` (pres. stem of `ستودن`) + [`-ش`](../word_formation.html#e-verbal-noun-from-the-present-stem) (nominalizer).
`بیست` _bīst_ "20" + `و` _o_ "and" + `سه` _se_ "3".

entries.meaning: to carry, take, bear; (فرمان بردن) to obey; (پیش بردن) to advance

forms.note: perfect `بیدار شده اند` "they have awakened" ([verse 23](#verse-23))

entries.meaning: following, pursuit — به دنبال / بدنبال: after, behind

forms.note: `دنبال کردن` "to pursue": `تو را دنبال می کنند` "they pursue thee" ([verse 23](#verse-23)); `به دنبال …` "in pursuit of, after" ([verse 23](#verse-23))

entries.family: نگاه _negāh_ look, glance (same root; نگه is the bound variant)

forms.note: Present stem `دار` _dār-_. As a plain verb `داشتن` drops `می-` in the present (`دارم` "I have"), but in the compound `نگه داشتن` it takes it: `نگه می دارم` "I will stop / hold back".

forms.desc: 1sg pres. `می دارم` _mī-dāram_ — `نگه می دارم` "I will stop" ([verse 23](#verse-23))

etym.prose: `بیش` bīš "more" + `-تر` -tar (comparative) → "more, greater."

forms.note: `بیشتر از این` "any further" ([verse 23](#verse-23))

etym.prose: from Arabic _safar_ "journey," root s-f-r "to travel."
from Arabic _idāma_ "continuation," root d-w-m "to last."
`بیست` _bīst_ "20" + `و` _o_ "and" + `پنج` _panj_ "5".

entries.meaning: Mosiah (king of the Nephites in Zarahemla)

etym.prose: Persian transliteration of English _Mosiah_, often linked to Hebrew _môšîaʿ_ "saviour, deliverer".
Middle Persian _padīruftan_ "to accept"; `بگوش دل نپذیرفته اید` = "ye have not hearkened."
